verdicts.flaw_description: The stated alternative cause actually reaches the units: "Rainfall in each block's season ran about a fifth above the year before, and every block lay in open ground, under no cover" - open, uncovered maize blocks receive that extra 20% rainfall, so a wetter season explains the 0.4-0.7 t/ha gains over the previous summer just as well as the drip line.

Two cases have the outcome measured before the boxes were installed: case one was "boxed 3 June" but fledging was counted "by 27 March", and case three was "boxed 2 November" but counted "by 24 September". The fledging gains in those plots therefore predate the intervention that is supposed to have caused them.

The competing cause is not blocked: "Class sizes at each school ran about a quarter below the year before, and every logged class took its English lessons as one whole group" - because English was taught to the undivided class, the ~25% smaller class size applied directly to the reading lessons, so smaller classes could produce the 5-9 point comprehension gains over the previous autumn term.

The measured population is narrower than the cohort the claim is about: "Pass rates cover the students who attended every block, and about a quarter of each cohort missed at least one block", so roughly 25% of each cohort is excluded from the post figures and the surviving full attenders are a self-selected, more diligent subgroup - the 4-8 point rise may be selection rather than the tutoring.
